status_reason: Material and target are known, but the silica cable cannot carry the MIR ATR band and the link length and fiber needed for an alternative are not supplied.
answer: The concept cannot be approved as proposed: the existing silica cable cannot transmit the 4000-2000 cm-1 mid-IR ATR band, so MIR ATR needs a CIR or PIR fiber. MIR reach over a link to another building is not documented in the sources, so the link length must be known before any feasibility decision. The first step is a laboratory test of MIR ATR on water-in-oil samples.

inline.headline: Test MIR ATR on water-in-oil samples with a ZrO2 ATR probe before any field link is built
inline.probe: ZrO2 ATR probe sealed in a PEEK shaft
inline.install: Lab trial first; field install point in the petroleum line not yet specified by the client
inline.fiber: CIR (1.1-6.5 um) or PIR (3-17 um) IR fiber; the existing silica cable is not usable for this band
inline.test_against: NIR transmission/transflection probe on the existing silica cable
inline.not_final_because: Link length, routing and operating conditions are unknown; MIR reach over a long link is not documented; the water range and accuracy are not defined.

problems.text: The existing silica cable cannot carry the MIR ATR signal: Vis-NIR silica transmits about 350-2400 nm, while the water-in-oil ATR spectra span 4000-2000 cm-1 (2.5-5 um).
Reach to another building is not shown for mid-IR fibers: the 100-300 m cables are described for low-OH silica (Vis-NIR), and the mid-IR fiber comparison is shown only for 2 m lengths.
Approval cannot be given yet: fiber type, link length, routing and conditions are needed, since method selection depends on these factors.
The water range and required accuracy are not stated; the only example in the sources covers 0.1-2.0 % water, gives no detection limit and no process conditions.

methods.why: The sources show water-in-oil absorbance rising with water content in 4000-2000 cm-1 with ZrO2 ATR probes; MIR ATR gives well-defined peaks and high selectivity, but needs a CIR or PIR fiber.

NIR works with standard glass optics and remote fiber probes, and can use the existing silica cable up to the stated 100-300 m; its water sensitivity in oil is not shown in the sources and must be tested.
Raman needs special probes but carries information complementary to MIR; it is only worth testing if MIR ATR and NIR fail.
Fluorescence relies on secondary emission from certain substances, mostly biological; most chemicals do not fluoresce, so it is unlikely to detect water in oil.

questions.q: What is the exact fiber link length and route from the line to the analyzer building?
questions.why: MIR reach over a long link is not documented, and this decides whether any MIR link is feasible.

questions.q: Is a new CIR or PIR IR fiber acceptable, or must the existing silica cable be reused?
questions.why: The silica cable cannot carry the MIR ATR band, so this choice changes the method.

questions.q: What water-content range and accuracy or detection limit do you need?
questions.why: The only example covers 0.1-2.0 % water and gives no detection limit.

questions.q: What are the operating conditions (temperature, pressure, flow, oil type)?
questions.why: The source example gives no process conditions, and probe choice depends on them.

questions.q: Can you supply petroleum samples with known water content for a first laboratory ATR test?
questions.why: Lab trials on the customer process are the first step in the AFS pathway.

experiment.objective: Check whether MIR ATR sees water in the petroleum samples across the client's range, before any link is designed.
steps: Prepare oil samples with known water levels across the client's range (the source example uses 0.1-2.0 %).
Record MIR ATR spectra over 4000-2000 cm-1 with a ZrO2 ATR probe.
Check whether absorbance increases with water content as in the source example.
Measure the same samples with an independent laboratory water analysis as reference.
Test a CIR or PIR fiber run at the required length to confirm transmission.
references: S02 p.20 (AFS pathway: lab trials first)
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria come from the client: the accuracy and range targets must be met on the independent laboratory water values.

pathway.key_features: Absorbance in 4000-2000 cm-1 increases with water content in the example spectra; key features still need to be identified on client samples.
pathway.path_reason: The link, fiber and water range are missing, so no tailored path can be chosen yet.

multispectral.combination: MIR ATR + NIR (contingency only, if the single-method test fails)
multispectral.why: The sources do not show a second method adding water information in oil; the single MIR ATR test must come first.
multispectral.test: Compare against MIR ATR alone on the same independent validation samples; a combination is only justified if it beats the best single method.

assumptions: The client's water range is similar to the 0.1-2.0 % example until the client states it.
Operating conditions are unknown and are not assumed for the first assessment.
The client's MIR ATR concept refers to water in the petroleum line itself, not to a gas or other phase.
